Autonomous gamebots hit by a player, bot or pet react like a player: a 0.3-2.5 s reaction delay (healers heal meanwhile; shorter for tanks and bold personalities), an area spell from a distance doesn't make its caster the bot's target, and healers cure a dotted group with the group cure. Companions and bots in your group are not affected. False keeps the immediate reaction.

When bot voices and bot memory are on: now and then (at most every 25-45 minutes) a bot sends you a tell: a friend saying hello or passing on news, a guildmate, or a solo bot of your level nearby asking to duo.
When bot voices are on: how much bots talk unprompted, from 0 (only answers) to 3 (very busy). 1 is a normal evening; it already rises and falls with how many bots are on and the hour.
Living Server: the build whose new defaults were last applied to this world's saved settings (set by the server; leave it alone).

Server life: about 4% of the Crafter bots are beggars. They live in their capital, beg you and passing bots for coin and loot (drag coin or an item onto one to give it), sell what they are given and hoard every copper. Ask anyone for gold or items and the beggars follow you around the city insulting you and defending their corners until you leave. Beggars never group or fight.

Server life: bots of your realm that see you solo a named monster, go on a kill streak in the frontier, get zerged or die to something silly tell /faction a few minutes later, and others react. Deeds build a reputation the realm talks about, and a nickname.

Server life: gamebots remember the bots they grouped with. Good runs make friends who look for each other when forming a party; bots who never showed up or wiped the group too often are kept apart until a long wait makes them take anyone.

Server life: pairs of bots live out dramas in /faction over days: a kill steal, a guild split, a romance, a ninja-loot trial. The same two bots play every episode; take a side in faction and the ending follows you.
Server life: now and then a gold spammer floods /faction until it is banned, and a few bots roleplay in thee-and-thou speech while the realm mocks them.
Server life: bots pass on rumours that are true: a rare named monster that just spawned, or an enemy keep whose guards are down. Go and see.
Server life: around Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year and other holidays on your PC's calendar, bots talk about them like 2003 players did and answer your holiday wishes.
Server life: one end-game raid in twenty has a bot who charges the final boss before the raid is ready, yelling his name, and the raid has to follow him in.
Does a monster with no faction bring others of its own kind (faction-less monsters with the same name) when it brings a friend? Monsters with a faction always use their faction.
